children: Infosys shares continued their downward slide on Tuesday, falling 1.07 percent to settle at Rs 1,027.40 per share on the NSE.
The stock has declined around 5 percent over the past five trading sessions.
The fall came amid a broader decline in IT stocks. The Nifty IT index fell up to 1 percent, with brokerage CLSA flagging subdued demand as a risk to the sector's medium-term earnings outlook.

"IT companies' management demand commentary going into the silent period for September quarter results remains cautious at best," CLSA said, adding that "weak macro fundamentals due to geopolitics, higher rates and inflation pose downside risk to earnings."

Prasenjit Paul, Fund Manager at 129 Wealth & Research and Analyst at Paul Asset, said the firm has maintained a bearish view on large-cap IT stocks since early 2026, as artificial intelligence is changing the traditional IT-services model faster than expected.

"Infosys itself says it is accelerating investments in AI, talent and platforms, while Q1 FY27 margin was still healthy at 21.1 percent. These investments can keep near-term growth and margin expansion under pressure," Paul said.
"The fundamental outlook is not positive. Technically also, the structure remains weak, with the stock around Rs 1,040 versus its 200-DMA near Rs 1,289," he said.

Paul said a short-term relief rally could be expected, but added that until the stock crosses and sustains above its 200-DMA, investors should avoid the stock, while existing investors can use short-term rallies to reduce exposure.

Meanwhile, CLSA said weak macroeconomic fundamentals, impacted by geopolitics, higher rates and inflation, have kept discretionary demand muted, implying more earnings-per-share downside risk, particularly for Infosys and Wipro.
"TCS too maintained a cautious stance while HCL's demand commentary remained the most resilient," the brokerage said.
CLSA, however, said order books and employee headcount are expected to remain largely stable, reducing the risk of extreme negative repercussions from AI rollouts on renewed deals and IT jobs.
The brokerage also said the banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) vertical continues to see resilient demand.
